overall_status: Published human-cohort reference fit; educational simulation, not clinical or independently validated

bone_anchor.model_use: Historical context only; superseded as the active calibration by the site-specific Sprint CON data.

sources.title: NASA: Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
sources.finding: NASA reports a broad average bone-density decline of 1–1.5% per month over four-to-six-month missions. This is not a site-specific fit or a uniform untreated cohort.

sources.title: NASA: Muscle Risk
sources.finding: NASA reports that adherent ISS crews with suitable exercise systems can return with small average muscle losses. Our fixed muscle-loss rate has not been fitted to those observations.

sources.title: NASA: OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview
sources.finding: This brief reviews exercise, medication and reconditioning evidence. It does not establish our numerical treatment effects, recovery half-lives or risk-score formula.

sources.title: NASA Human Research Roadmap: Fracture 1
sources.finding: The closed gap's rationale does not establish a large clinical effect on fracture healing. Much of the earlier evidence used animal models. Our injury slowdowns are hypothetical, not measured human healing factors.

sources.title: English et al. (2020): NASA Sprint study
sources.finding: Tables 1, 4 and 5 provide site-specific bone, leg lean-mass and relative peak-oxygen measurements for a standard-exercise group of 17 people, with mean mission duration 165 days. The app fits these aggregate endpoints under explicit assumptions.

sources.title: Scott et al. (2023): Multisystem exercise outcomes
sources.finding: A larger human cohort shows substantial outcome variation. Some participants overlap with earlier work, so this is context, not independent validation. Individual data require a NASA archive request.

sources.title: Moore et al. (2014): Peak oxygen uptake
sources.finding: A separate historical cohort had early-flight cardio changes the current smooth curve does not reproduce. This documented mismatch limits interpretation of daily predictions.

sources.title: NASA countermeasure studies: ARED exercise (Smith 2012) and ARED + bisphosphonate (LeBlanc 2013)
sources.finding: Crews using the ARED resistance device returned with hip and pelvis bone density unchanged from preflight, unlike crews on the older iRED; adding a bisphosphonate gave further protection. The app checks that its plans rank the same way. Effect sizes are not fitted.

parameters.label: Hip bone density
parameters.note: Reproduces a ratio of CON group means at its postflight test window. Daily shape, reference routine and recovery correction are assumptions; this is a descriptive fit, not predictive validation.

parameters.label: Back bone density
parameters.note: Reproduces a ratio of CON group means at its postflight test window. Daily shape, reference routine and recovery correction are assumptions; this is a descriptive fit, not predictive validation.

parameters.label: Leg lean tissue proxy
parameters.note: Reproduces a ratio of CON group means at its postflight test window. Daily shape, reference routine and recovery correction are assumptions; this is a descriptive fit, not predictive validation. DXA lean tissue is not isolated muscle or strength; its reported change was not significant.

parameters.label: Peak aerobic fitness
parameters.note: Reproduces a ratio of CON group means at its postflight test window. Daily shape, reference routine and recovery correction are assumptions; this is a descriptive fit, not predictive validation.

parameters.label: Minimum retained tissue
parameters.note: Simulation floors prevent indefinite decay; they are not established physiological lower bounds.

parameters.label: Exercise, nutrition and medication effects
parameters.status: development assumption; direction checked against NASA studies
parameters.note: Stronger resistance exercise and adding a bisphosphonate reduce modeled hip loss, the same direction NASA crews showed (Smith 2012; LeBlanc 2013). The size of each effect is still assumed; the per-site tables needed to fit it were not openly accessible.

parameters.label: Injury loss and healing
parameters.note: All severity durations, local loss multipliers and microgravity slowdowns are hypothetical scenario settings, not validated return-to-duty estimates.

parameters.label: Postflight recovery
parameters.note: Exponential recovery is illustrative. Recovery depends on the person, tissue and rehabilitation; these half-lives are not fitted.

parameters.label: Age, fitness and sex adjustments
parameters.note: Age, sex and fitness multipliers are neutral. Aggregate data do not establish individual susceptibility; crew profiles do not produce invented demographic effects.

parameters.label: Shaded forecast ranges
parameters.note: Sensitivity envelopes around the scenario, not statistical confidence intervals.

parameters.label: Colored risk flags
parameters.note: Heuristic display cutoffs, not NASA operational standards, calibrated probabilities, or clearance for medication, EVA or landing.

limits: Four endpoint rates are fitted to published group means under the reference routine, not to individual astronaut records.
A fit to its own source values is not independent validation or a measure of prediction accuracy.
Postflight measurement timing is retained; bone/lean scans at days 7–14 use day 11 as a chosen fit approximation.
Exercise dose, food, medication effects, injury curves and recovery half-lives remain scenario assumptions. More minutes need not mean better real-world outcomes.
Daily cardio curves miss early-flight adaptation reported in a separate NASA cohort.
Leg lean tissue is not strength; no measured fracture probability or operational clearance is produced.
All destinations use ISS-based rates. Short/long missions and Moon/Mars are extrapolations.
Shaded ranges and body colors are illustrative sensitivity displays, not confidence intervals or anatomy measurements.
No clinical validation, user study or independent individual-level predictive validation has been completed.
